response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-18
CLINICAL INDICATION: Surveillance. History of treated colon adenocarcinoma. Assess for new pulmonary nodules.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. A. Rahimi (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-05-14
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same view on both. Minor difference in image processing and contrast between the two films, and the current film is framed slightly smaller within the image. This limits judging subtle change in density of small nodular opacities or fine lung markings. It does not prevent gross comparison of size and position.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- No finding is flagged time-sensitive (routine). Findings to review first: F1 small dense nodular opacity at the lateral edge of the left hilum; F2 small dense focus at the right hilum. Both are stable versus prior but uncharacterized.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central. Carina and main bronchi unremarkable at this resolution. Lungs well inflated. No consolidation, collapse or reticular interstitial change. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. F1: small dense, well-defined rounded nodular opacity at the lateral edge of the left hilum. Its high density is consistent with a calcified nodule or granuloma, but calcification is not confirmed on these films. No new satellite opacity around it. F4: mildly prominent bronchovascular markings in the right lower zone with no focal consolidation. This is indeterminate because the two blind reads disagreed (reported by one of two reads). The breast shadow overlies this zone.
- Mediastinum / hila: Upper mediastinum not widened. Aortic knuckle visible. Mild convexity of the left heart border below the aortic knuckle, in the region of the pulmonary artery segment. Hila normal in position, left slightly higher than right. F2: small dense focus overlying the right hilum, which fits a vessel seen end-on or a small calcified hilar node. No one-sided hilar enlargement.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles sharp. No visible pleural line, pleural thickening, pneumothorax or effusion.
- Heart: F3: cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly enlarged on PA, with a prominent left heart border. Heart borders are sharp. No measurement was made.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive bone lesion seen at this resolution. Clavicles and shoulders intact. No soft tissue gas. No lines, tubes, ports, pacemaker or surgical clips. A small external radiopaque object projects at the lower image edge on the patient's right, below the diaphragm. Below the diaphragm: both domes well defined, gastric bubble under the left dome, and no crescent of gas under the right dome.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No new pulmonary nodule is seen by eye in either lung on the current film compared with the prior. No other interval change is identified.
- Unchanged: F1 left hilar nodular opacity is present in the same position with similar size, shape and density. F2 right hilar focus is similar. F3 cardiac silhouette is similar in size and shape on both PA films. F4 right lower zone markings are similar. The prior report states lungs clear with no focal opacity. The prior film itself shows F1 and F2, which the prior report does not mention. The stable status is based on comparing the two images, not on the prior report.

RECIST 1.1: RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the small dense left perihilar nodule calcified (consistent with a granuloma), a non-calcified nodule, or a vessel seen end-on? | Reason: Small nodule on a frontal X-ray only. The image is low resolution and compressed, so calcification and margins cannot be confirmed. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS and compare with any older films. CT chest if it has not been characterized before. (F1, read A)
- Is the small dense right hilar focus a vessel end-on or a calcified hilar node? | Reason: Small density overlapping hilar vessels on a frontal film alone. Fine detail is limited at this resolution. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with a lateral view if available. CT chest if characterization is needed. (F2, read A)
- Is the heart truly enlarged, and is the left heart border convexity a prominent pulmonary artery or a chamber contour? | Reason: The silhouette is borderline on a frontal film and no measurement is made here. A frontal film alone does not show chamber configuration. | Recommend: Radiologist to measure the cardiothoracic ratio on both PA films in PACS. Lateral view or echocardiography if clinically relevant. (F3, read A)
- Is the small left hilar nodule calcified and benign in character? | Reason: The nodule is small and seen on frontal films alone. The image is compressed and low resolution, so calcification and margin cannot be confirmed. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS and compare with any older studies. If it has not been characterized before, CT chest. (F1, read B)
- Is the small dense focus at the right hilum a vessel end-on or a calcified node? | Reason: A small density over hilar vessels on a frontal film cannot be separated from normal vascular overlap. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest if characterization is needed. (F2, read B)
- Is the cardiothoracic ratio above the normal limit? | Reason: The heart size is borderline by eye, and no measurement is made on image files without a pixel scale. | Recommend: The radiologist measures the cardiothoracic ratio in PACS on both PA films. (F3, read B)
- Is there a lesion behind the heart or behind the domes of the diaphragm? | Reason: Only frontal films were provided, and these areas are hidden by overlap. | Recommend: Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern. (no related finding, read B)

IMPRESSION:
1. F1: small dense, well-defined nodular opacity at the lateral edge of the left hilum, stable versus prior 2026-05-14 by image comparison. Not mentioned in the prior report. Calcification is not confirmed and the lesion remains uncharacterized (see CAN'T DETERMINE). Confirm in PACS given the history of treated colon adenocarcinoma.
2. F2: small dense focus at the right hilum, stable versus prior. It may be a vessel end-on or a small calcified node, which is not determined. Not mentioned in the prior report.
3. No new pulmonary nodule is seen by eye on this surveillance film. Small nodules and the areas behind the heart and diaphragm cannot be excluded on a single frontal film at this resolution.
4. F3: cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal to mildly enlarged, similar to prior. Not measured. Cardiothoracic ratio to be measured in PACS.
5. F4: mildly prominent right lower zone bronchovascular markings, indeterminate because the two blind reads disagreed. Similar to prior, with no focal consolidation.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review source images in PACS and compare F1 and F2 with any older films.
- CT chest if F1 has not been characterized before, or if characterization of F2 is needed. No interval is specified in the findings. Timing is per attending.
- Radiologist to measure the cardiothoracic ratio on both PA films in PACS. Lateral view or echocardiography if clinically relevant.
- Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern, for the areas behind the heart and diaphragm.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
